title: HEO and ORiS partner to advance satellite detection and tracking for space-based laser operations
summary: HEO and ORiS partner to advance satellite detection and tracking for space-based laser operations
body_markdown:
BREMEN, Germany, \[18 November, 2026\] – HEO and ORiS have signed a Memorandum of Understanding at Space Tech Expo Europe to advance satellite detection and tracking for future in-orbit wireless power transmission.


The collaboration will use existing and on-demand HEO imagery and associated insights to develop and validate ORiS detection and tracking algorithms. The companies will also assess the compatibility of HEO imaging and analysis with ORiS’ planned in-orbit demonstration architecture.


The partnership will explore the potential for a dedicated in-orbit observation campaign and future joint demonstrations.


“Accurately understanding the position, orientation and characteristics of objects in orbit is fundamental to future space operations. We’re excited to work with ORiS to combine HEO’s space-based imaging expertise with their laser technology, demonstrating another way non-Earth imaging can enable new capabilities and missions in space,” said Hiranya Jayakody, CTO and Co-Founder of HEO.


“For decades, satellites have been designed to operate with the resources they carry at launch. We believe the next generation of space infrastructure will move beyond that limitation,” said Domenico Edoardo Sfasciamuro, CCO and Co-Founder of ORiS. “Our collaboration with HEO combines advanced space-based inspection capabilities with our vision of delivering energy to spacecraft remotely, laying the groundwork for a new generation of in-orbit services. This partnership represents an important step towards making space infrastructure more capable, resilient, and sustainable.”


‍


**About HEO**


HEO is building the intelligence layer for space. We image objects in orbit on demand, turning existing satellites into inspection platforms and building our own sensors where coverage gaps remain. Our software automates tasking, capture and analysis, turning imagery into insight about the condition, configuration and behaviour of objects in orbit. HEO operates internationally, with offices in Australia, France, Japan, the United Kingdom and the United States. Our goal is to make any image in the Solar System available on demand.

**About ORiS**


ORiS is a deep-tech company based in Italy developing laser-based wireless power transmission systems for space. ORiS is building the technology for an in-orbit energy distribution grid, designed to give satellites access to additional power. Its first in-orbit demonstration, planned for 2027, will test wireless power transmission over 10 meters. The company is also planning a follow-on mission to deliver power to a satellite from several kilometers away. Its mission is to power a multiplanetary future.
